question.problem: If a curve $C$ is given by $y={e}^{x}\operatorname{sin}⁡x,$ calculate the slope of the tangent line to the curve at the point where $x=\pi .$
question.worked_solution:
We differentiate using the product rule. Let $u(x)={e}^{x}$ and $v(x)=\operatorname{sin}⁡x.$ Then, we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x}={e}^{x},\,\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}=\operatorname{cos}⁡x.
$$

Applying the product rule gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =u\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}+v\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x} \\  & ={e}^{x}\cdot \operatorname{cos}⁡x+(\operatorname{sin}⁡x)\cdot {e}^{x} \\  & ={e}^{x}(\operatorname{cos}⁡x+\operatorname{sin}⁡x).\end{aligned}
$$

To find the slope of the tangent line, we now substitute $x=\pi $ into the formula and get

$$
\begin{aligned}{\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x}|}_{x=\pi } & ={{e}^{x}(\operatorname{cos}⁡x+\operatorname{sin}⁡x)|}_{x=\pi } \\  & ={e}^{\pi }(-1+0) \\  & =-{e}^{\pi }.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the slope of the tangent line is $-{e}^{\pi }.$
